# Fairstay Length of Stay (`fairstay-length-of-stay`)

The case management weekly meeting list for skilled nursing-home stays: late or due NOMNC notices, residents the team calls custodial still on a skilled payer, discharges past their date, clinical reviews overdue, managed care authorizations ending with no plan, and Medicare day 20 and day 100 coming up. Resident identifiers are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairstay Length of Stay never delivers notices to residents or families.**

Fairstay ver 1 · Case management · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairstay-core`](../fairstay-core)

```bash
npx -y fairstay-length-of-stay demo
npx -y fairstay-length-of-stay mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional Cedar Hollow skilled residents for the meeting on 17 March 2026. Planted:

- R1401: last covered day 18 March and no NOMNC, so it is already late.
- R1402: last covered day 21 March, so the NOMNC is due by 19 March, and Medicare day 20 falls on 20 March.
- R1403: Medicare day 100 falls on 29 March.
- R1404: managed care, planned discharge 12 March, last reviewed 3 March, and an authorization ending 19 March with no plan.
- R1405: the team says no longer skilled, but the resident is still on managed care.
- R1406 is early in a Medicare stay, and R1407 is on Medicaid, so both are left alone.

[`rules-typo.json`](fixtures/rules-typo.json) misspells a setting, so the check refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `los_check` | List skilled residents who need a decision or a notice this week, most urgent first. | runs |
| `los_write_report` | Write los-weekly-meeting.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and los-weekly-meeting.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/los). | runs |
| `los_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `los_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `los_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `los_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `notice_deliver` | Fairstay Length of Stay never delivers notices to residents or families. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `los_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `census` (required) | Census under --root: residents, payers and dates |
| `stays` (required) | Case management log under --root: last covered day, NOMNC date, planned discharge, last review, still skilled (Y/N), authorization end, next plan, Part A days used earlier |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: review_days, nomnc_warn_days, day20_warn_days, day100_warn_days, auth_warn_days |
| `as_of` | Meeting date (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairstay-length-of-stay inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Census (`census`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `facility` | text | Facility, Facility Name, Building, Location, Fac, Center |
| `from` (required) | date | From, Start, Start Date, Effective Date, Begin Date, From Date, Admit Date, Census Date |
| `to` | date | To, End, End Date, Thru, Through, Thru Date, Through Date, To Date |
| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `payer_type` | text | Payer Type, Payor Type, Payer Class, Payer Category, Pay Type |
| `level` | text | Level, Level of Care, Care Level, Rate Type, Rate Level, Room Type, Accommodation, RUG |
| `bed_status` | text | Bed Status, Status, Census Status, Action, Census Action, Leave Type |
| `room` | text | Room, Room Bed, Bed, Room/Bed, Unit |

### Case management log (`stays`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `last_covered_day` | date | Last Covered Day, Last Covered Date, Skilled End, Cut Date |
| `nomnc_given_on` | date | NOMNC Given, NOMNC Date, NOMNC Delivered, NOMNC |
| `planned_discharge` | date | Planned Discharge, Anticipated Discharge, Expected Discharge, Target Discharge |
| `last_review` | date | Last Review, Last Clinical Review, Last Meeting, Reviewed On |
| `skilled` | text | Skilled, Skilled Need, Still Skilled, Meets Skilled Criteria |
| `auth_end` | date | Auth End, Authorization End, Auth Through |
| `next_plan` | text | Next Plan, Plan, Discharge Plan, Next Payer |
| `part_a_days_used` | number | Part A Days Used, Prior SNF Days, Benefit Days Used |

## Settings file (`los_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `review_days` | Flag residents not reviewed for this many days (default 7) |
| `nomnc_warn_days` | List NOMNCs due within this many days (default 5) |
| `day20_warn_days` | Warn this many days before Medicare day 20 (default 7) |
| `day100_warn_days` | Warn this many days before Medicare day 100 (default 14) |
| `auth_warn_days` | Warn this many days before a managed care authorization ends (default 3) |

## Memory

`los_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `los_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `meeting_note` | is shown with results. It never changes a check. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairstay-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairstay-length-of-stay": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairstay-length-of-stay",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairstay-length-of-stay -- npx -y fairstay-length-of-stay mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairstay-length-of-stay tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairstay-length-of-stay sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairstay-length-of-stay inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairstay-length-of-stay call los_check '{"census":"<census>","stays":"<stays>"}'
fairstay-length-of-stay eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairstay-length-of-stay demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
